title: (No AI) Anthropic’s IPO filing reveals its strategy for keeping enterprise customers hooked

content: Anthropic’s S-1 shows more than half of its $100,000-plus customers now use both the Claude Platform and a first-party app, a cross-selling playbook reminiscent of Amazon that’s making enterprise customers stickier.

title: (No AI) SpaceX locks in $40B GPU financing deal with Apollo
dc:creator: Aditya Mehta
content: SpaceX has locked in a binding commitment for roughly $40 billion in financing to pay for AI chips and related data center equipment, the company disclosed in a regulatory filing Monday. In a statement, SpaceX called it the “largest committed GPU financing” ever.

title: (No AI) The RealReal won’t let AI agents hog designer clothing
author: Mia Sato
content:
![Shopping basket with an 8-bit effect.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/STKS539_AI_AGENTS_SHOPPING_E.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

The RealReal, a secondhand luxury fashion consignment retailer, said it's updating its bot defense system, effectively making it harder for AI agents to shop on its site.

The change comes days after _The Verge_ [reported](https://www.theverge.com/report/1015811/ai-shopping-agents-blocked-amazon-the-realreal-target-meta-muse) that an AI agent could be used to take advantage of The RealReal's item reserve system. On the retailer's website, an item goes "on hold" and is unavailable for other customers to buy for 20 minutes once it's placed in a user's shopping cart. Using Meta's Muse, _The Verge_ was able to instruct the AI agent to continuously re-add The RealReal listings in a shopping cart as soon as the 20-minute hold had expired, effectively block …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/news/1018713/meta-muse-agentic-shopping-ai-the-realreal)

title: (No AI) Five weird details from Anthropic’s IPO filing
author: Robert Hart
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/STK202_DARIO_AMODEI_CVIRGINIA_C.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Anthropic has [finally filed](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1018476/anthropic-ipo-details-s1-filed-sec) its S-1 prospectus with the SEC, a [document](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2130357/000162828026067168/anthropicpbc-sx1.htm) designed to give investors a look under the hood of its business, from how much its executives are making and plans for spending its IPO billions to the risks that could derail its ambitions.

At more than 300 pages, there's a lot to unpack, and some of the disclosures have not previously been reported. Here are some of the biggest things that jumped out to us from our first pass:

## **It pays to be an Amodei**

Sibling co-founders Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei are the two most highly-paid executives at Anthropic, according to the filing. Last year, CEO Dario's compensation …
